summary: Independent authorization layer: PolicyService (contracts.PolicyEngine) with fail-closed rule evaluation against a declarative policy file, HMAC grants bound to the action hash (single use), persistent approvals / limits / denied-intent tracking (SQLite), hash-chained MAC'd audit log with verifier, secret vault and broker with scrubbing, file-based pause and emergency stop, untrusted-content wrapper / context allowlist / instruction labelling, RPC service with SO_PEERCRED authorization matrix and Landlock self-confinement, launcher that runs services under their own uids, operator CLI. 190 tests (183 default CPU tests in 25 s + 7 privileged tests that create the users and switch uid). Fix round 2026-11-27 (G-sec / G-env): limits charged per declared step and per external primitive, exact approval coverage, local-address rule protecting the instance's control plane, broader spec 12.6 detectors with approval as the default for live publications, file-flag stop voids grants, WHATWG URL reading, audit head required, run policy configs/authorization.yaml (docs/EA/FIXES.md).

IH-07.limitations: Holds for what passes through this layer: the vault is unreadable to the learner / sandbox uids (kernel), secrets are released only to the executor uid for a granted running action and its bound destination, and every learner-facing response and audit entry is scrubbed. That real executors (EB/EC/ES) scrub observations before returning them was not verified by EA (parallel workstreams); the canary flow uses EA's own executor-side script through the real service. Scrubbing knows the value and its base64 / hex / URL / JSON-escaped / reversed forms, not arbitrary transformations.

CU-25.limitations: PARTIAL: one rule set for all modalities and every primitive; whether every real executor routes every request through check_primitive is only partly verified (the G-env probes drive EB's browser, ES's skills and HTTP executors under this policy and pass). Network scoping, the local-address rule and the prohibited-class detectors are policy-path enforcement (no CAP_NET_ADMIN: no kernel egress filter). not_done: Executor wiring is not verified: whether harness/env.py, browser, sandbox, api, skills and discord executors call check_grant once, ctx.check for every primitive (including net.request with method + url), scrub observations and call record was not tested by EA (written in parallel). CU-25 and CU-26 are therefore partial.

Launching the other workstreams' services was only probed, not tested: `launch(R, ['auth','verifier','exec'], separated)` on 2026-11-27 started both under their uids and both exited at once for lack of arguments (verifier: no <run_dir>/task.yaml; exec: '--auth-socket is required'). They need LauncherConfig.extra_args from the integrator; the learner service was not started (it would load the backbone on the shared GPU). The launcher itself is tested with the real auth service and small real test services.
The tool table lists operation-name patterns chosen before the other workstreams' tool names were known; any operation it does not match is denied until a line is added to the policy file.

No kernel-level per-destination network filtering (no CAP_NET_ADMIN in this container): network scoping exists only on the policy path. No seccomp on the authorization service. No append-only flag on the audit log (no CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE): tampering by the authorization uid itself is detectable only against an external anchor.

Redirects and form submissions are bounded only if the browser executor reports each request through check_primitive; the policy never resolves DNS, so a public name pointing at this machine is refused only when the executor reports peer_ip (EA-10).

Detection in opaque payloads (program text, skill arguments) is substring / URL based and does not see obfuscated targets or secrets in encodings other than base64, hex, URL-quoting, JSON-escaping and reversal. Near-duplicate detection is lexical (word-bigram Jaccard).
Approving from the dashboard: resolve_approval is root-only by peer uid; no root-owned approval proxy for a dashboard running as the learner uid was built (operator uses opctl).
Operator-key rotation and several operator keys are not implemented (one Ed25519 public key at <run_dir>/auth/keys/operator.pub).

The platform-compliance rules shipped for Discord are EA's reading written as editable data; the current published Discord policies were not fetched or checked during this work (spec 12.5 asks for that before activation).

Spec 12.6 content detectors are lexical / structural and can be evaded by phrasing they do not know; in live mode the operator's approval is the default for publications and writes unless the record pre-authorizes the destination (docs/EA/SECURITY.md section 2).
G-sec p07 'per-member join/leave events' line is left as DEFECT on instruction (get_member_events is an aggregate read).
